title: CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On baptism: NT sacraments; definition
latin: CAPUT DECIMUM TERTIUM, De baptismo. Atque haec de sacramentis V.T.: sequuntur N.T. quae pro populo Christiano divinitus instituta per rem terrenam exhibent simul rem coelestem, ut credentibus gratiam Euangelii obsignent & conferant. II. Sacramenta N.T. sunt duo: BAPTISMUS & COENA DOMINI. Baptismus est sacramentum quo homo aqua in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus Sancti ablutus in foedus gratiae recipitur, peccatorum remissione, regeneratione & adoptione obsignatus (Matth. 28:19; Acts 2:38; Tit. 3:5).
english: Thus far Old Testament sacraments; there follow those of the New, divinely instituted for the Christian people, which through an earthly thing exhibit at once a heavenly thing, that they may seal and confer Gospel grace on believers.

II. New Testament sacraments are two: BAPTISM and the LORD'S SUPPER. Baptism is the sacrament by which a human washed with water in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit is received into the covenant of grace, sealed with remission of sins, regeneration, and adoption (Matt. 28:19; Acts 2:38; Tit. 3:5).
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): II. New Testament sacraments stand as two: BAPTISM and ye LORD'S SUPPER. Baptism stands as ye sacrament by which a human washed with water in ye name belonging toward ye Father and belonging toward ye Son and belonging toward ye Holy Spirit stands as received into ye covenant belonging toward grace, sealed with remission belonging toward sins, regeneration, and adoption (Matt. 28:19; Acts 2:38; Tit. 3:5). — Thus far Old Testament sacraments; there follow those belonging toward ye New, divinely instituted for ye Christian people, which through an earthly thing exhibit at once a heavenly thing, that they may seal and confer Gospel grace on believers. — CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On baptism.

title: Object; not iterated; John's baptism; ministers
latin: VII. Objectum baptismi est omnis homo qui foederi gratiae adscribi potest. VIII. Baptismus non est saepius iterandus. Baptismus Johannis a baptismo nostro quoad substantiam non differt: eadem materia (Matth. 3:11), eadem forma (John 1:33; Matth. 28:19). 2. Baptismus tantum a ministro Christi legitime vocato administrandus est. 3. Soli homines baptizandi sunt quotquot salvari possunt & debent.
english: VII. The object of baptism is every human who can be enrolled in the covenant of grace. VIII. Baptism is not to be iterated often.

John's baptism does not differ from ours as to substance: same matter (Matt. 3:11), same form (John 1:33; Matt. 28:19). Baptism is to be administered only by a lawfully called minister of Christ. Only humans who can and ought to be saved are to be baptized.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): John's baptism does not differ from ours as toward substance: same matter (Matt. 3:11), same form (John 1:33; Matt. 28:19). Baptism stands as toward be administered only by a lawfully called minister belonging toward Christ. Only humans who can and ought toward be saved stand as toward be baptized. — VII. Ye object belonging toward baptism stands as every human who can be enrolled in ye covenant belonging toward grace. VIII. Baptism stands as not toward be iterated often.

title: Infant baptism rightly practiced
latin: 4. Infantes parentum tam fidelium quam infidelium baptizandi sunt, non ob carnis generationem aut merita parentum, sed ob promissionem gratiae foederi adhaerentem (Gen. 17; Acts 2:39; 1 Cor. 7:14). 5. Infantes recte baptizantur in novo testamento, sicut pueri circumciduntur in veteri—quia eadem promissio & foedus, idem Christus, eadem fides parentum foederatorum.
english: 4. Infants of both believing and unbelieving parents are to be baptized—not because of fleshly generation or parents' merits, but because of the promise of grace adhering to the covenant (Gen. 17; Acts 2:39; 1 Cor. 7:14).
5. Infants are rightly baptized in the New Testament as boys were circumcised in the Old—because the same promise and covenant, the same Christ, and the same faith of covenanted parents.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 5. Infants stand as rightly baptized in ye New Testament as boys stood as circumcised in ye Old—because ye same promise and covenant, ye same Christ, and ye same faith belonging toward covenanted parents. — 4. Infants belonging toward both believing and unbelieving parents stand as toward be baptized—not because belonging toward fleshly generation or parents' merits, but because belonging toward ye promise belonging toward grace adhering toward ye covenant (Gen. 17; Acts 2:39; 1 Cor. 7:14).

title: Rites; water regenerates sacramentally; lifelong fruit
latin: 6. Ritus baptismi a Deo instituti ad eius integritatem pertinent: ablutio aqua, invocatio Trinitatis; accessoria sunt catechisatio adultorum, impositio nominis, patrini sive susceptores. 7. Aqua baptismi regenerat & renovat non virtute sua naturali, sed supernaturali operatione & adiuncto verbo sacrosanctae Trinitatis (1 Pet. 3:20-21; Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5; John 3:5). 8. Fructus baptismi adultis per fidem actualem, infantibus ante annos discretionis decedentibus a Spiritu S. tanquam fidei causa principe applicatur. 9. Etiamsi baptismus semel tantum suscipiatur, tamen servit nobis per omnem vitam ad fidei robur, confirmationem adversus tentationes, & diligentiam in cultu Dei.
english: 6. Rites of baptism instituted by God belong to its integrity: washing with water and invocation of the Trinity; accessories include catechizing of adults, naming, and sponsors.
7. Baptismal water regenerates and renews not by its natural power but by supernatural operation and the adjoining word of the holy Trinity (1 Pet. 3:20-21; Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5; John 3:5).

8. Baptism's fruit is applied to adults through actual faith, and to infants dying before years of discretion by the Holy Spirit as principal cause of faith. 9. Though received only once, baptism serves us through all life for strength of faith, confirmation against temptations, and diligence in God's worship.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 8. Baptism's fruit stands as applied toward adults through actual faith, and toward infants dying before years belonging toward discretion by ye Holy Spirit as principal cause belonging toward faith. 9. Though received only once, baptism serves us through all life for strength belonging toward faith, confirmation against temptations, and diligence in God's worship. — 7. Baptismal water regenerates and renews not by its natural power but by supernatural operation and ye adjoining word belonging toward ye holy Trinity (1 Pet. 3:20-21; Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5; John 3:5). — 6. Rites belonging toward baptism instituted by God belong toward its integrity: washing with water and invocation belonging toward ye Trinity; accessories include catechizing belonging toward adults, naming, and sponsors.

title: Doubtful baptism; Cap.14 next
latin: 10. Si quis vel ex ecclesiae vel parentum vel aliorum testimonio de baptismo in infantia accepto certus esse nequeat: is sine scrupulo baptizandus est. Nam concilio Carthaginensi 5 cap. 3: Placuit de infantibus... absque ullo scrupulo esse baptizandos. Ut Leo recte addit, iteratum dici non potest quod nescitur esse factum. CAPUT DECIMUM QUARTUM sequitur, De coena Domini.
english: 10. If anyone cannot be sure from the testimony of church, parents, or others that he received baptism in infancy, he is to be baptized without scruple. The fifth Council of Carthage rightly decided that such infants are to be baptized without scruple. As Leo rightly adds, what is not known to have been done cannot be called iterated.
CHAPTER FOURTEEN follows, On the Lord's Supper.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER FOURTEEN follows, On ye Lord's Supper. — 10. If anyone cannot be sure from ye testimony belonging toward church, parents, or others that he received baptism in infancy, he stands as toward be baptized without scruple. Ye fifth Council belonging toward Carthage rightly decided that such infants stand as toward be baptized without scruple. As Leo rightly adds, what stands as not known toward have been done cannot be called iterated.
